title: A genomic future for fisheries assessments
content:
Abstract

Traditional fisheries stock assessments incorporate life history data (e.g., mortality, growth, maturity), indices of abundance, and catch data into models to determine stock status and estimate biological reference points. However, obtaining these data in an accurate and timely manner can be challenging. While genetic techniques have been used for over 50 years to identify independent stocks, recent genomic innovations now allow for the generation of multiple stock assessment data inputs. Specifically, DNA extracted from non-lethally sampled tissue (e.g., fin clips) can be analyzed to monitor population structure and levels of connectivity, to estimate absolute abundance, to assess the age composition of landed or discarded catch, and to estimate sex ratios. Through standardized, adaptable, and minimally invasive methods to collect data necessary for robust stock assessments, genomic tools have the potential to provide a relatively comprehensive and cost-effective approach for long-term monitoring. The enhanced integration of next-generation genomic data into stock assessments will improve the accuracy and efficiency of fisheries assessment and management, ultimately supporting the sustainable use of marine resources.
